subject: Sara Curtis stole a world record. Kaylee wants it back.
preheader: Plus: Brendan Hansen's wild injury, Kate Douglass eyes sub-23, and your Monday set.
heroHeading: Good morning swimmers and happy Monday
heroTeaser: Kaylee McKeown just found out what it feels like to lose a world record to Sara Curtis, and her response is the most competitive thing you'll read all week.
outroLine: That's the week in the water. Happy swimming,

workout.dateLabel: Mon, Sep 14 · Distance freestyle aerobic endurance in the pool, rotational power & glute stability on land

swimSet.title: Today's Swim Set
swimSet.description: A 3,000-yard aerobic freestyle builder focused on smooth rhythm and an efficient catch, finishing with a strong negative-split block to sharpen your back-half speed.

lift.title: Today's Lift
lift.description: A core and stability session targeting rotational power and glute stability, with emphasis on movements that carry over directly to freestyle and backstroke.

newsItems.title: McKeown lost her 50 back WR. She's not taking it lying down.
newsItems.body: Kaylee McKeown had her 50-meter backstroke world record broken by Sara Curtis this summer, and her reaction was about as fierce as you'd expect: she says it fuels the fire and she's all for taking people down.

newsItems.title: Brendan Hansen tore both patellar tendons in a cannonball contest
newsItems.body: Six-time Olympic medalist and USA Swimming National Junior Team Director Brendan Hansen tore both patellar tendons during a July 4th cannonball contest and is now five weeks into rehab. A reminder that the pool is sometimes the safest place to be.

newsItems.title: Kate Douglass has a number in mind: 22-point-something
newsItems.body: Kate Douglass confirmed in a SwimSwam podcast with Mel Stewart that breaking the 23-second barrier in the 50-meter freestyle is on the table, and she's already mapping the road to LA 2028.

newsItems.title: Texas lands two top-ranked recruits early
newsItems.body: The University of Texas will get a December head start with top-ranked 2027 recruit Luka Mijatovic and highly rated Ian Call both arriving on campus before the new year.

athlete.name: Sara Curtis
athlete.photoCredit: Photo: Agnagnas, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
athlete.bio:
Sara Curtis, born on 19 August 2006 in Savigliano, Italy, is an Italian competitive swimmer specializing in sprint freestyle and backstroke events. She was born to an Italian father and a Nigerian mother and trains under coach Thomas Maggiora with Team Dimensione Nuoto.

Curtis holds the long course world record in the 50 metre backstroke. At the 2022 World Junior Championships she won silver medals in the 50 metre freestyle, 4x100 metre medley relay, and 4x100 metre mixed medley relay, along with a bronze in the 50 metre backstroke. At the 2022 European Junior Championships she won gold in the 4x100 metre freestyle relay and bronze medals in the 50 metre freestyle and 4x100 metre medley relay.
